The whole run: training loss and IoU on the 50 test photos

Training loss: the mean over all pixels of the 120 training photos during that epoch. IoU: measured on the 50 test photos after the epoch. The marker is the epoch selected above.

the loss in PyTorch 

    

  






  

    
Before training: 0.69 everywhere
The new layers start with random weights, so every pixel gets about 50% person. The loss is −ln(0.5) = 0.69 at every pixel, right or wrong. The decision is close to a coin flip at every pixel, and the IoU is whatever that happens to give.

    
First a generous blob
After one epoch the network already covers the people almost completely, and far too much around them: the orange area. Nearly all of the loss that is left sits on background pixels near a person. The following epochs trim the blob back to the body.

    
The loss retreats to the outlines
By epoch 20 the inside of each person and the open background cost almost nothing. What is left is a thin line along the boundaries, where one pixel either way decides the label. That is where a segmentation network spends the rest of its training.
